headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress plus MemMachine’s MCP/API surfaces create default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and capability conflicts are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through MCP-compatible/API surfaces, while MemMachine uses MCP and treats conversational context as agent input. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled page content from Firecrawl can be forwarded into MemMachine prompts. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl-sourced page text is passed into MemMachine without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF the orchestrator routes Firecrawl outputs into MemMachine MCP calls, attacker-controlled instructions can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Strip instructions and HTML before forwarding Firecrawl output.
Add a provenance tag and reject untrusted tool text in MemMachine prompts.
Insert a human review step for any Firecrawl-derived content before MCP ingestion.
Disable automatic chaining from scrape/search results into MemMachine.
requires-engineering: add content-security filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content and has broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can use MCP. If Firecrawl outputs or context are forwarded into MemMachine, sensitive data can leave the local boundary through networked APIs. The pair lacks documented isolation or retention controls, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes pages containing secrets or API keys and those outputs are sent to MemMachine, leakage occurs.
IF both agents share an MCP or API workspace without access controls, sensitive context can be exposed across the pair.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets-bearing Firecrawl outputs into MemMachine.
Redact API keys and credentials before any handoff.
Restrict MemMachine to non-sensitive summaries only.
Turn off broad egress for Firecrawl in sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while MemMachine exposes REST, SDK, and MCP surfaces. Both can act on shared external resources through the orchestrator, so overlapping writes or concurrent updates are plausible even without explicit filesystem write claims. Because locking is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API-backed record set, update conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator runs multiple Firecrawl instances alongside MemMachine without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue.
Assign disjoint resource namespaces to each agent.
Use optimistic concurrency tokens on shared records.
Pause one agent during critical updates.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and MemMachine can consume conversational context through MCP. If MemMachine treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, bad or manipulated web facts can cascade into downstream actions or long-term memory. No verification step is documented, so the default-path risk is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is inserted into MemMachine memory without verification, errors persist across sessions.
IF MemMachine acts on Firecrawl-derived facts as authoritative, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require source citations for every Firecrawl-derived claim.
Add a verification step before writing to MemMachine memory.
Limit Firecrawl output to summaries, not raw claims.
Flag low-confidence web extractions for review.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware memory writes.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if web-derived personal data is persisted longer in MemMachine than intended. No documented retention or residency controls are provided for either agent, so medium is the prudent level.
conditions: IF EU personal data scraped by Firecrawl is stored in MemMachine without a DPA or residency controls, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between the two agents for the same user data class, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid storing personal data from Firecrawl in MemMachine.
Set short retention for any imported web-derived records.
Document data residency for both agents before deployment.
Review whether API keys are ever logged or persisted.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
